title: The River Mumma's Gift
summary: A kind girl from Guyana meets the River Mumma who grants her a special gift of always knowing when the river is safe.

pages.text: There was once a girl named Amani who lived by the Essequibo River in Guyana.
pages.illustration: A young girl standing by a wide beautiful river

pages.text: Every day she watched the river shimmer in the sunlight.
pages.illustration: Golden sunlight sparkling on water

pages.text: The elders told stories of the River Mumma who lived deep below.
pages.illustration: An old woman telling stories to children around a fire

pages.text: They said she had a golden comb in her hair.
pages.illustration: A mermaid-like figure with a shining golden comb

pages.text: One evening Amani saw something glowing in the water.
pages.illustration: A soft golden glow beneath the river surface

pages.text: It was the River Mumma rising up!
pages.illustration: The River Mumma emerging from the water gracefully

pages.text: The River Mumma spoke: You are kind to the river. Take this gift.
pages.illustration: The River Mumma holding out a small glowing pebble

pages.text: The pebble would glow when the river was calm and dim when it was dangerous.
pages.illustration: A glowing pebble in Amani palm

pages.text: Amani used the gift to keep her village safe for many years.
pages.illustration: Amani holding the pebble up, village behind her

pages.text: The End. The river always takes care of those who are kind.
pages.illustration: Amani sitting peacefully by the river at sunset

title: Dilly Doubles and the Carnival King
summary: Dilly Doubles helps save Carnival when the Carnival King loses his special steelpan.

pages.text: It was Carnival Monday in Trinidad and the whole island was buzzing with excitement.
pages.illustration: Colorful Carnival costumes and flags everywhere

pages.text: Dilly Doubles was getting ready for the parade with his friends.
pages.illustration: A cheerful boy in a colorful costume holding a flag

pages.text: But the Carnival King Papa Steelpan was very upset.
pages.illustration: A tall man in a golden costume looking worried

pages.text: My special steelpan is gone! he cried.
pages.illustration: Papa Steelpan holding empty hands up in despair

pages.text: Without the steelpan there could be no Carnival!
pages.illustration: Sad people standing around with no music

pages.text: Dilly thought and thought. Where could it be?
pages.illustration: Dilly with his hand on his chin thinking hard

pages.text: He remembered seeing a monkey run off with something shiny.
pages.illustration: A monkey carrying a shiny pan into the trees

pages.text: Dilly followed the monkey tracks into the Paramin hills.
pages.illustration: Footprints leading up a green hillside

pages.text: There was the monkey playing the steelpan beautifully!
pages.illustration: A monkey sitting on a branch playing a steelpan

pages.text: Dilly traded the monkey a big bag of bananas for the steelpan.
pages.illustration: Dilly handing over bananas while the monkey hands back the pan

pages.text: Carnival was saved and everyone danced in the streets!
pages.illustration: A massive Carnival celebration with dancing and music

pages.text: The End. Sometimes the best adventures start with a missing thing.
pages.illustration: Fireworks over a Carnival stage at night

title: The Chickcharney's Lesson
summary: A boy from Andros Island in the Bahamas learns respect when he meets the mysterious Chickcharney birds.

pages.text: In the pine forests of Andros Island lived strange birds called Chickcharnies.
pages.illustration: Owl-like bird creatures sitting in pine trees

pages.text: They had big eyes and could turn their heads all the way around.
pages.illustration: A Chickcharney turning its head in a circle

pages.text: A boy named Devon was exploring the forest.
pages.illustration: A curious boy walking through tall pine trees

pages.text: He saw a Chickcharney and laughed at its funny face.
pages.illustration: Devon pointing and laughing

pages.text: The Chickcharney was not amused.
pages.illustration: The Chickcharney looking stern with arms crossed

pages.text: Suddenly Devon could not find his way home!
pages.illustration: Devon looking lost among identical pine trees

pages.text: Every path led him back to the same tree.
pages.illustration: Devon walking in circles looking confused

pages.text: The Chickcharney appeared again and tilted its head.
pages.illustration: The Chickcharney looking at Devon with one big eye

pages.text: Devon said: I am sorry for laughing. Please help me.
pages.illustration: Devon bowing his head respectfully

pages.text: The Chickcharney nodded and showed him the path home.
pages.illustration: The Chickcharney leading Devon through the trees

pages.text: The End. Always respect the creatures of the forest.
pages.illustration: Devon waving goodbye to the Chickcharney from his doorstep

title: The Mermaid of Carlisle Bay
summary: A Barbadian boy meets a mermaid who teaches him to protect the coral reef.

pages.text: Kwame loved fishing in Carlisle Bay in Barbados.
pages.illustration: A boy on a small wooden boat in turquoise water

pages.text: One dawn he saw something shimmering near the reef.
pages.illustration: A silvery glow under the water near coral

pages.text: It was a mermaid with scales like blue diamonds!
pages.illustration: A beautiful mermaid with blue scales sitting on a rock

pages.text: She looked sad. The coral is dying she said.
pages.illustration: Bleached white coral around the mermaid

pages.text: Kwame promised to help. He told all the fishermen.
pages.illustration: Kwame talking to a group of fishermen on the beach

pages.text: They stopped dropping anchors on the reef.
pages.illustration: Fishermen carefully placing anchors on sand not coral

pages.text: Kwame organized a beach cleanup with his school.
pages.illustration: Children picking up trash from the beach

pages.text: Slowly the coral came back to life.
pages.illustration: Colourful coral growing back with little fish swimming around

pages.text: The mermaid returned and gave Kwame a pearl.
pages.illustration: The mermaid handing over a glowing white pearl

pages.text: Thank you for caring for our ocean she whispered.
pages.illustration: The mermaid smiling and sliding back into the water

pages.text: The End. The sea takes care of those who take care of it.
pages.illustration: Kwame holding the pearl up to the sunrise

title: Steelpan Sam and the Rhythm of the Rain
summary: Steelpan Sam discovers that the rain has its own music and creates a new song for the village.

pages.text: Sam loved playing his steelpan.
pages.illustration: A boy with a big smile playing a shiny steelpan

pages.text: He played every day in the yard.
pages.illustration: Sam playing outside his house with palm trees

pages.text: One day it started to rain.
pages.illustration: Grey clouds and raindrops falling

pages.text: Sam could not play outside anymore.
pages.illustration: Sam looking sad through a window at the rain

pages.text: He listened to the rain on the roof. Drip drop!
pages.illustration: Raindrops hitting a tin roof

pages.text: It sounded like music!
pages.illustration: Musical notes floating from the raindrops

pages.text: Sam got his steelpan and played along.
pages.illustration: Sam playing his pan matching the rain rhythm

pages.text: Drip drop ding dong!
pages.illustration: Rain and steelpan notes dancing together

pages.text: The whole village came to listen.
pages.illustration: People gathering outside in the rain smiling

pages.text: The End. Music is everywhere if you listen.
pages.illustration: A rainbow over the village with musical notes

title: Anansi and the Mango Tree
summary: Anansi the spider tries to keep all the mangoes for himself, but learns that sharing makes everyone happy.

pages.text: Anansi was sitting under the biggest mango tree in Jamaica.
pages.illustration: A spider sitting under a tall mango tree full of golden mangoes

pages.text: He wanted all the mangoes for himself!
pages.illustration: Anansi hugging the tree trunk protectively

pages.text: But the mangoes were too high to reach.
pages.illustration: Anansi stretching his legs up the tree, looking frustrated

pages.text: Along came Tanty Spice with a big stick.
pages.illustration: A warm grandmother figure carrying a long bamboo stick

pages.text: She knocked the mangoes down one by one.
pages.illustration: Mangoes falling like golden rain

pages.text: Anansi tried to grab them all but they rolled away!
pages.illustration: Anansi chasing rolling mangoes in every direction

pages.text: The children came running and helped pick them up.
pages.illustration: Happy children gathering mangoes in baskets

pages.text: Anansi shared the mangoes and everyone had a feast.
pages.illustration: A big picnic under the mango tree with Anansi and children

pages.text: From that day, Anansi always shared.
pages.illustration: Anansi smiling, handing a mango to a small child

pages.text: The End. Remember: sharing makes the sweetest fruit.
pages.illustration: Sunset over the mango tree with hearts floating up

title: The Legend of the Silk Cotton Tree
summary: A St Lucian boy learns about the history and spirits of the ancient silk cotton tree from his grandmother.

pages.text: In a village in Saint Lucia there stood an ancient silk cotton tree.
pages.illustration: A massive tree with a wide trunk and spreading branches

pages.text: It was taller than every house and older than memory.
pages.illustration: The tree towering over small village houses

pages.text: Jaden grandmother told him the tree was sacred.
pages.illustration: An old woman pointing up at the tree reverently

pages.text: She said our ancestors gathered under it long ago.
pages.illustration: Shadowy figures of ancestors gathered under the tree at dusk

pages.text: They told stories and made plans beneath its branches.
pages.illustration: People in olden clothes sitting and talking under the tree

pages.text: Some said spirits lived in the trunk.
pages.illustration: Glowing shapes inside the trunk of the tree

pages.text: Jaden was curious but a little scared.
pages.illustration: Jaden looking at the tree with wide eyes

pages.text: One night he heard whispering from the tree.
pages.illustration: Jaden in bed hearing soft whispers on the wind

pages.text: He was brave and went closer.
pages.illustration: Jaden tiptoeing toward the tree in moonlight

pages.text: The whispers were just the wind in the leaves!
pages.illustration: Leaves rustling in a gentle breeze with moonlight

pages.text: But he felt a warm peace like a hug from the past.
pages.illustration: Jaden leaning against the trunk with closed eyes and a smile

pages.text: The End. The roots of our history make us strong.
pages.illustration: The silk cotton tree at dawn with Jaden walking home

title: Papa Bois and the Lost Fawn
summary: Papa Bois, guardian of the forest, helps a lost baby deer find its mother in the Trinidad mountains.

pages.text: Deep in the Trinidad forest lived Papa Bois.
pages.illustration: A wise old man with deer antlers standing among tall green trees

pages.text: He cared for all the animals.
pages.illustration: Papa Bois feeding birds and rabbits

pages.text: One day a baby fawn was lost.
pages.illustration: A small spotted fawn looking sad under a big leaf

pages.text: The fawn cried for its mama.
pages.illustration: Tears rolling down the fawn face

pages.text: Papa Bois heard the cry.
pages.illustration: Papa Bois with his hand to his ear listening

pages.text: He followed the footprints in the mud.
pages.illustration: Small hoof prints in brown mud

pages.text: They walked past the river.
pages.illustration: Papa Bois and fawn walking beside a sparkling river

pages.text: They walked past the bamboo grove.
pages.illustration: Tall bamboo swaying in the wind

pages.text: Mama deer was waiting by the big silk cotton tree!
pages.illustration: A mother deer nuzzling her baby

pages.text: The End. Papa Bois always watches over the forest.
pages.illustration: Papa Bois waving goodbye under a full moon

title: The Rolling Calf of Green Bay
summary: A brave Jamaican girl overcomes her fear of the legendary Rolling Calf.

pages.text: In the hills of St Ann Jamaica lived a girl named Zara.
pages.illustration: A girl standing on a green hillside

pages.text: The elders warned about the Rolling Calf that came out at night.
pages.illustration: An old man telling stories by lamplight

pages.text: They said it had fiery eyes and dragged heavy chains.
pages.illustration: A shadowy figure with glowing red eyes in the dark

pages.text: Zara was afraid to walk home after sunset.
pages.illustration: Zara walking quickly with her eyes wide

pages.text: One night she heard the chains clanking behind her.
pages.illustration: Zara looking over her shoulder frightened

pages.text: Her heart beat fast. But she remembered what Tanty said.
pages.illustration: Zara clenching her fists and standing tall

pages.text: Tanty said: Fear is just a shadow. Turn around and face it.
pages.illustration: Tanty Spice pointing a finger firmly

pages.text: Zara turned around and stood very still.
pages.illustration: Zara facing the dark with her chin up

pages.text: The Rolling Calf stopped. Its eyes were just fireflies!
pages.illustration: Glowing fireflies arranged like eyes in the bushes

pages.text: The chains were just old pots clanking in the wind.
pages.illustration: Old pots hanging from a tree swinging in the breeze

pages.text: Zara laughed and walked home brave and proud.
pages.illustration: Zara walking home with a big smile under the stars

pages.text: The End. Most fears disappear when you face them.
pages.illustration: Zara waving at her house with fireflies all around

title: Mango Moko and the Garden Race
summary: Mango Moko and his friends race to grow the biggest garden but learn that working together is better.

pages.text: Mango Moko lived in Grenada the Spice Isle.
pages.illustration: A cheerful boy standing on a hill overlooking green fields

pages.text: He loved growing things more than anything.
pages.illustration: Mango tending to plants in a garden

pages.text: One day he challenged his friends to a garden race.
pages.illustration: Mango and three friends standing with gardening tools

pages.text: Whoever grows the most food wins!
pages.illustration: A starting line with plants and vegetables

pages.text: Everyone worked hard on their own gardens.
pages.illustration: Each child working separately in their own plot

pages.text: But Mango Moko garden was not doing well.
pages.illustration: Mango looking at droopy plants sadly

pages.text: His friend Kai had too many tomatoes but no carrots.
pages.illustration: Kai surrounded by tomatoes looking puzzled

pages.text: His friend Nia had too many carrots but no tomatoes.
pages.illustration: Nia surrounded by carrots looking puzzled

pages.text: Tanty Spice said: Why not share and grow together?
pages.illustration: Tanty with a knowing smile pointing to both gardens

pages.text: They combined their gardens into one big one!
pages.illustration: All the children working together in one big garden

pages.text: They grew more food than ever before and shared it all.
pages.illustration: Baskets overflowing with vegetables and happy faces

pages.text: The End. Together we grow stronger.
pages.illustration: A beautiful community garden at sunset

title: R.O.T.I. and the Lost Words
summary: R.O.T.I. the teaching robot helps children find words that have gone missing from their island dictionary.

pages.text: R.O.T.I. was a friendly robot who loved teaching words.
pages.illustration: A cute round robot with a screen face showing letters

pages.text: He lived in the Likkle Legends library.
pages.illustration: A cozy library with books and the robot in the middle

pages.text: One morning some words from the dictionary went missing!
pages.illustration: A dictionary with blank spaces where words should be

pages.text: Liming was gone. Bacchanal was gone. Fetê was gone!
pages.illustration: Blank pages with question marks

pages.text: R.O.T.I. rolled out to find them.
pages.illustration: The robot rolling down a village street on wheels

pages.text: He found liming at the coconut vendor cart.
pages.illustration: Friends hanging out at a coconut cart with the word floating above

pages.text: He found bacchanal at the Carnival mas camp.
pages.illustration: A busy costume workshop with the word floating above

pages.text: He found fetê at the pan yard rehearsal!
pages.illustration: A steelpan practice session with the word floating above

pages.text: The words had gone to the places where they belong!
pages.illustration: All three words glowing above their respective places

pages.text: R.O.T.I. put them back in the dictionary.
pages.illustration: The robot carefully placing words back into the book

pages.text: The End. Words are alive — they live where we use them.
pages.illustration: A happy dictionary with all words glowing

title: Tanty Spice and the Pepper Sauce Secret
summary: Tanty Spice teaches a little girl how to make the perfect pepper sauce but the secret ingredient is love.

pages.text: Tanty Spice was famous for her pepper sauce.
pages.illustration: A grandmother in a colourful kitchen surrounded by bottles

pages.text: Everyone said it was the best in Trinidad.
pages.illustration: People lining up outside Tanty house

pages.text: Little Maya wanted to learn the secret.
pages.illustration: A small girl looking up at Tanty with big eyes

pages.text: Tanty said: First you need the reddest scotch bonnet peppers.
pages.illustration: A basket of bright red peppers

pages.text: Then you need garlic and shadow benny herbs.
pages.illustration: Fresh garlic and green herbs on a wooden table

pages.text: Maya chopped and mixed and stirred.
pages.illustration: Maya with an apron stirring a big pot

pages.text: But it did not taste right. Something was missing.
pages.illustration: Maya tasting from a spoon and frowning

pages.text: Tanty smiled and said: The secret ingredient is love.
pages.illustration: Tanty hugging Maya from behind

pages.text: Maya closed her eyes and thought about how much she loved her family.
pages.illustration: Maya stirring with her eyes closed and a smile

pages.text: Then she tasted again. It was perfect!
pages.illustration: Maya tasting and her eyes going wide with joy

pages.text: The End. The best recipes are made with love.
pages.illustration: Maya and Tanty holding up jars of pepper sauce together
